object_description: two near-identical volumes pushed together at a corner
design_condition: Two near-identical volumes are loosely arranged around the existing school, spanning connected planted outdoor areas and adapting ancillary spaces to the site’s slope.

positive.statement: The outdoor areas span an arch to the existing school building.

position.rationale: The top view clearly shows open areas spanning between and around the two volumes.

positive.statement: The location and separation of the entrances keep the building entrances clear along the street.

position.rationale: Entrances are directionally approximated along the clear street-facing edge.

positive.statement: The small multi-purpose hall can be converted into a foyer extension and functions as a spacious entrance.

position.rationale: The internal hall and foyer are not distinguishable; the central lower zone is used.

positive.statement: The staircase to the cloakrooms is architecturally appealing and appropriately designed for school sports.

position.rationale: The staircase is internal and approximated within the visible building mass.

positive.statement: The lighting of the adjoining rooms is otherwise above average.

position.rationale: Adjoining rooms are not exposed, so a representative mid-height side zone is selected.

positive.statement: The ground-floor kindergartens are oriented south and have a visual relationship with the common playground.

position.rationale: South-facing ground-level zones and adjacent open space are directionally supported by the views.

positive.statement: The continuous planted band connects the new buildings with the existing school building.

position.rationale: A connecting low-level strip between volumes is the best available landscape anchor.

positive.statement: The large sports and playing fields correspond to the loose setting of the two buildings.

position.rationale: Large open ground zones around the loose masses represent the playing fields.

positive.statement: The chosen construction method can be assumed to be sustainable.

position.rationale: Sustainability applies to the construction approach without a locatable geometric feature.

positive.statement: The facade design and loose setting are appropriate to the village context.

position.rationale: Repeated facade bands and the loose envelope are visible across the elevations.

negative.statement: Simultaneous occupancy of the large and small multi-purpose halls is not possible.

position.rationale: Hall interiors are not represented distinctly; the central lower building zone is used.

negative.statement: The double hall is lit only through a high opening on the north side, producing an uneven distribution of light.

position.rationale: The north facade and upper-level region provide a directional approximation for the opening.

negative.statement: The location and separation of the second staircase required for fire safety are undecided and obscure the floor-plan organization.

position.rationale: The fire stair is internal and cannot be identified in the sampled exterior.

negative.statement: The delivery route crosses the access area, creating conflicts during events.

position.rationale: A peripheral ground-level route is used because deliveries are not separately modeled.

negative.statement: The new buildings are expected to have low construction costs, but their maintenance costs are comparatively high.

position.rationale: Cost judgment concerns the buildings generally and has no spatially locatable referent.

negative.statement: The wide central zone and sometimes large classroom depths make the building dimensions questionable for school use and create unsatisfactory daylight situations.

position.target: wide central zone and classroom depths
position.rationale: Central depth and broad internal zones are approximated from the loose massing and elevation spans.
